purpose: This is the normative authorization policy for the shipped Courtside API. OpenAPI defines the transport shape; this policy defines who may perform each operation, which resource attributes narrow that permission, and which protected fields each projection may read or write.

principals.description: A caller without an authenticated Courtside session.
An authenticated account holding the ordinary member role.
An authenticated account holding the trainer role. The start-up warm-up passes this role without an account to preview a series.
An authenticated account holding the sport-director role.
An authenticated account holding the youth-director role.
An authenticated account holding the groundskeeper role.
An authenticated account holding the treasurer role.
An authenticated account holding the instance administrator role. The start-up warm-up passes this role without an account to write a booking it rolls back.
An authenticated account restricted to replacing its issued one-time password.

A password-verified pending browser session has no authenticated roles or account privileges.

operationRules.description: Build metadata, the API document, login status and idempotent logout are available without permanent account authority.
Login accepts credentials from an anonymous or existing browser only through the dedicated form fields and never returns them.
Account recovery by name mails a single-use code to the address on the account and changes nothing, so the answer is the same whether or not the name belongs to anybody.

Redeeming a reset code is the only anonymous operation that changes an account. The code names the account, so no caller identity is read and none is required; an unknown, spent or withdrawn code is refused with the same problem type.
The address path reminds each account registered to an address of its own name by mail and changes no credential, session or account state.
Public club configuration, facilities and calendar occupancy are readable without account authority through deliberately bounded response projections.
An account carrying an issued credential may replace it but may perform no ordinary authenticated operation first.
Permanent accounts may read their sessions and notification centre, mark their own notifications read, and change only the locale and message and channel choices attached to their own account.
A permanent account may prove or replace only its own password through the dedicated credential operations.
A permanent account may terminate its own sessions; ending every session or another browser additionally requires a recent password proof.
Permanent accounts may discover active booking cards admitted by their roles for future booking requests.
Permanent accounts may discover the active participant-card types available when naming a booking participant.
Permanent accounts may search the bounded current-member projection used to name a participant in their own booking request.
A permanent account may create or preview bookings only with a booking card admitted by its roles and the current resource state.
A permanent account sees its own bookings and participations and may mutate only an owned booking or its own participation; administrators retain the documented booking override.
A permanent account granted account tasks for a dependant has new credentials issued to the dependant's account after a recent full-password proof.

A permanent account lists the dependants it acts for today, and for each one reads its bookings, books in its name, cancels the bookings it holds and reads its notification centre, each only where the relationship grants that action.
A permanent account joins, reads, leaves and accepts only its own waitlist entries; joining and accepting pass the booking-card and rule checks of a booking.

A permanent account offers and withdraws the open place only of a booking it holds, and lists and takes only open places it may take itself; taking a place passes the booking-card check and the membership type's booking eligibility, not the rules that judge a booking itself.
A permanent account sees booking management data only when one of its roles manages the booking card; administrators may manage every card.
Series cancellation and movement require ownership of the series or a booking-card management role; administrators retain the documented override.
Ordinary administration requires an enabled permanent account carrying ADMIN; operation-specific validation and state guards still apply.
Correcting a person's identity or address requires ADMIN and a recent full-password proof.
Creating or correcting account security, terminating one account's sessions and creating, changing, ending or removing a guardian relationship requires ADMIN and a recent full-password proof.
Changing roles or enabled state requires ADMIN, recent authentication and preservation of at least one enabled administrator.
Terminating every account session requires ADMIN and recent authentication and also ends the caller's current session.
Executing a reviewed import requires ADMIN, recent authentication and ownership of a current preview whose source and roster state still match.
Running a retention preview requires ADMIN, recent authentication and ownership of a current, unexpired preview.
Changing or resetting the wording of a message requires ADMIN and recent authentication, because the wording includes what credential and reset-code mails say.
Public admission to a password-first pending ceremony, not unrestricted authentication.
Holder-private MFA status and credential labels.
Factor and recovery-code changes require current holder identity and recent full proof.
Obtain an account/session-bound assertion challenge to renew expired full proof.
Only the two coarse administrative factor-state flags.
Fresh MFA administrator proof plus an explicit external identity check.
Public admission still requires the mailed single-use code and an acceptable permanent password.

decisions.title: Public request boundary
decisions.rule: Only explicitly public routes admit an anonymous caller; all other shipped operations require a valid server-side session. MFA login routes still require the password-verified pending ceremony, and controlled recovery still requires its valid mailed code.

decisions.title: Permanent account gate
decisions.rule: Ordinary account operations require an authenticated, enabled account whose issued credential has already been replaced by a permanent password.

decisions.title: Initial password gate
decisions.rule: The initial-password authority reaches only password replacement and loses all authority when that replacement succeeds.

decisions.title: Administrator gate
decisions.rule: Every route below /api/admin requires ADMIN and rejects anonymous, initial-password and every non-admin product role before the operation runs.

decisions.title: Own account scope
decisions.rule: The authenticated account identifier selects profile identity, session, locale, appointment reach, message-choice, channel-choice and notification state; callers cannot supply another account identifier to these operations, and a notification id outside the account answers as not found. MFA state follows immutable principal identity rather than a reused username.

decisions.title: Credential write-only boundary
decisions.rule: Passwords are accepted only by their dedicated credential workflows, never returned in a response and never accepted by account administration.

decisions.title: Booking card role and state
decisions.rule: A booking card must be active and admit at least one actor role; ADMIN bypasses the card role list but not facility availability or invariant checks. The start-up warm-up also acts here as an in-process caller without an account or request input, and it rolls back every write it makes.

decisions.title: Booking and participation ownership
decisions.rule: Personal queries derive identity from the current account; cancellation requires the booking owner or ADMIN, check-in requires the booking owner and withdrawal removes only the current person's participation, from a booking that is not cancelled; a person the booking never named is answered as not found before its status is read. A notification describes and links a booking only to its owner or a current participant. The start-up warm-up also acts here as an in-process caller without an account or request input, and it rolls back every write it makes.

decisions.title: Guardian delegation
decisions.rule: Every guardian action reads, at its point of use, the relationship between the authenticated account's person and the named dependant on the club's today. Without one holding, or while the guardian's account is disabled or the dependant holds no account, the dependant answers as not found; an action the relationship does not grant is refused by name. A booking is held by the dependant's account and measured against the dependant and the dependant's roles without the administrator override; cancellation reaches only a booking the dependant holds, in the dependant's name. Reading messages marks nothing read.

decisions.title: Waitlist entry ownership
decisions.rule: The current account selects which waitlist entries are read, left and accepted; another account's entry answers as not found, no response names another waiting account or a position, and a reserved court refuses every other account's booking unless an admin books it or it is closed, which withdraws the offer.

decisions.title: Partner invitation holder and taker
decisions.rule: Only the account holding a booking publishes or withdraws its open place; another account's booking answers as not found. Open places are listed to and taken by an enabled account acting as its own person, not barred from booking, whose roles the card admits, that neither holds the booking nor already plays in it, checked again under the booking row lock; any other invitation answers as not found, and no listed place names a person or a booking.

decisions.title: Participant card availability
decisions.rule: Participant-card discovery returns active cards only; it has no booking-card role allowlist or administrator override.

decisions.title: Managed booking scope
decisions.rule: Managed listings and details contain only bookings whose card names one of the actor roles as a managing role; ADMIN sees every card. The start-up warm-up also acts here as an in-process caller without an account or request input, and it rolls back every write it makes.

decisions.title: Series ownership and management
decisions.rule: Moving or cancelling a series requires its creator, a role that manages the series booking card, or ADMIN; the selected occurrence scope is preserved.

decisions.title: Recent full authentication proof
decisions.rule: Sensitive operations require full proof no older than five minutes. Accounts without MFA prove their password; enrolled accounts prove their password plus an unused TOTP/recovery code or valid native WebAuthn assertion. Password-only repetition cannot renew an enrolled account proof. Factor enrollment and changes use the same current-account and recent-proof gate.

decisions.title: Administrator continuity
decisions.rule: The last enabled administrator cannot remove its ADMIN role or disable its account; another enabled administrator makes the same transition permissible.

decisions.title: Import preview ownership and state
decisions.rule: Only the administrator who created a current, unexpired preview may execute it, and execution rechecks its source and roster fingerprints before any write.

decisions.title: Retention preview ownership and state
decisions.rule: Only the administrator who created a retention preview may run it, once, before it expires and while the periods it applies are unchanged.

decisions.title: Import preview read projection
decisions.rule: Every administrator may read a stored preview; after its retention expires, personal change details and ignored columns are removed while non-personal counts and hashes remain.

decisions.title: Public response projection
decisions.rule: Public configuration and calendar responses use dedicated DTO projections and never widen to administrative configuration, roster or another person's booking details.

decisions.title: Participant directory projection
decisions.rule: Participant search returns only the stable person identifier and display name of current members other than the searching person, never roster, account, address or membership administration fields.

decisions.title: Administrative response projection
decisions.rule: Administrative DTOs may expose the documented roster and operational fields to ADMIN only; credentials remain absent and subject access omits other people's booking data.

decisions.title: Password-first pending MFA login
decisions.rule: MFA login entry points admit a request before full authentication, but succeed only for its password-verified pending session and unexpired account/session/purpose/epoch-bound challenge. Only a valid factor consumes that challenge, rotates the session, grants roles and records sign-in. Generic malformed requests do not prove successful authorization.

decisions.title: Private MFA holder scope
decisions.rule: An authenticated permanent account selects its MFA state by immutable principal ID. Changes refresh and lock that account, require its current epoch, enabled state and no pending rescue. A native credential may be renamed or removed only by its holder. Holder-private labels, usage times and credential identities never enter administrative or ordinary export projections.

decisions.title: MFA method and ceremony proof
decisions.rule: First enrollment requires recent password proof; changes to an enrolled account require recent password plus an existing factor. TOTP activates only after a valid unused step. Native WebAuthn registration/assertion checks origin, RP, challenge, user verification, credential owner and monotone counter. Codes and setup secrets appear only in their holder generating response; only verifiers or account-bound ciphertext remain stored.

decisions.title: Administrative MFA projection
decisions.rule: Only ADMIN may read another account MFA status. That projection contains only enabled and recovery-pending flags, with no method identities, labels, usage metadata, setup secret or recovery code.

decisions.title: Controlled MFA account rescue
decisions.rule: Rescue initiation requires a currently enabled ADMIN with active MFA, fresh full proof and explicit external identity confirmation. It revokes sessions and blocks ordinary credential routes while retaining factors. Public redemption requires the single-use mailed code, matching username/current address/security epoch, unexpired state, persistent guess budget and acceptable permanent password. Only successful redemption removes factors and clears the block. Operator rescue and separately audited address correction require identity confirmation. Ordinary credential and reset-code jobs queued before rescue must finish permanently without replacing recovered credentials or leaving a usable reset code, including delayed and retried jobs. New requests after completed rescue follow the ordinary policy.

fieldRules.description: A username and password are accepted only by form login and never occur in an API response.

Session identity fields describe only the account attached to the current session and become absent, empty or false for an anonymous caller. Pending status exposes available methods without granting identity or roles.
Opaque revocation handles and normalized browser metadata are visible only to the account that owns those sessions.
The issued credential replacement is accepted only by the initial-password operation and is never part of a response projection.
The current and replacement passwords are accepted only by the own-password operation and never appear in a response projection.
Password and optional second-factor proof are accepted only by reauthentication and never projected back. An enrolled holder must supply a valid second factor.
Current member lookup exposes only the identifier and display name needed to add that member to a booking.
The public allocation projection withholds booker identity; participant surnames and generic card identity appear only on the authenticated viewer's own booking.
A booking note and personal booking identifiers are returned only through the current account's own booking projection.
A guardian reads only the names, granted actions and end of the relationships that hold for them today, and no other personal data of a dependant.
Participant display names and internal notes appear only in the detail of a booking whose card the actor may manage.
Names and email addresses can be introduced only through the dedicated administrative person creation workflow.
Correcting a person's names or email address requires both administrator authority and recent full-password proof.
An account identifier and its initial roles are writable only through account creation after a recent administrator password proof.
An account username is replaceable only through its dedicated operation after a recent administrator password proof.
Replacing account roles requires recent administrator proof and preserves at least one enabled administrator in the instance.
Replacing account enabled state requires recent administrator proof and preserves at least one enabled administrator in the instance.
Full person, membership and account state is confined to administrative roster responses and never contains a password or reusable session credential.
Every period of a person's membership, with its type and dates, is confined to administrative roster responses.
Who may act for whom, with both names, the granted actions and the dates, is confined to administrative roster responses.
Credential lifetimes and the no-membership rule assignment are visible only in the administrative configuration projection.
Credential lifetimes, reminder timing and the no-membership rule assignment can be changed only through the administrator configuration operation.
A participant's person identifier or guest name is accepted only as part of the current account's authorized individual booking request.
A recurring booking note is accepted only as part of the current account's authorized series preview or creation request.
Audit actor data, parameters and resolved subject names are available only to administrators through the audit log.
Message identifiers and recipient metadata are available only to administrators through the message log.
Potentially personal message fragments and trace identifiers are accepted only from administrators through the private operational-log request body.
Redacted operational messages and trace identifiers are available only to administrators through the bounded operational-log projection.
The subject-access projection is administrator-only and contains data about exactly the selected person while excluding other people's booking notes and identities.
External member identifiers and their person links are confined to dedicated administrator reference operations.
Previewed person values and possible matches are visible to administrators until the preview retention expires and the personal change set is removed.
The name a caller submits to recover an account. It is written and never read back: the operation returns no body, so a caller learns nothing about whom it matched.
The code a caller redeems and the password it sets. Both are written only: the operation returns no body, and neither field occurs in any response projection.
The address a caller submits to be reminded of the names registered to it. The names travel to that address and never into the response.
A participant's person identifier or guest name and a note are accepted only as part of the current account's own waitlist entry, checked as a booking request would be.
Waitlist entry identifiers, state and booking are returned only to the account that joined; the reserved-slot projection names an entry only to its holder.
An invitation identifier, the handle that takes an open place, is returned only to an account that may take that place.
A reserved slot names its entry only to the account holding the offer and nobody's identity to anyone else.
A person's list of missed bookings is visible only to ADMIN; the attendance outcome of a single booking appears to whoever may manage that booking.
Which former members a retention run cannot remove yet, and why, is visible only to ADMIN in the preview that judged them.
Only the holder reads factor state, remaining-code count, native credential IDs, private labels and usage times.
The setup secret and QR URI go only to the requesting holder during recent-proof enrollment, never to administrators or exports.
Plaintext recovery codes appear once, only in their holder generating response. Status, administrators and exports never return them.
A code completes only the current pending password-first session and is never returned.
The holder supplies an unused code to confirm its pending setup; the response never echoes the proof.
The holder alone receives its bound user identity, challenge and excluded credential identifiers.
Challenge and allowed credential identifiers belong only to this bound browser/account ceremony.
Challenge and allowed credential identifiers belong only to this bound browser/account ceremony.
Native attestation, client data, raw credential IDs and extensions are accepted only for this holder enrollment ceremony and never echoed.
The private human label is writable only while enrolling this holder credential.
A label can be renamed only on the current holder credential with fresh full proof.
The native assertion authenticates only its saved pending session challenge and is never echoed in a response.
Administrators read only enabled and recovery-pending flags for the selected account. No method identity, private label or credential leaves this projection.
An active MFA administrator confirms the external identity check only after fresh full proof.
Username, mailed rescue code and permanent password are accepted by the bound rescue workflow and never returned.
A static access code opens a door on its own, so only the administrative access point projection carries it.
Only an administrator sets or removes the static access code of an access point.
A booking's static access codes travel only in the booker's own and a granted guardian's booking projection, and only until its validity window ends.
A player sees a booking's static access codes only in their own participation projection, and only until its validity window ends.
